## TL;DR

I resumed Task #1184 from its existing checkpoint, reviewed the shared Agent
card and QA test, completed the four-page keyboard pass with headless Playwright,
and fixed an accessible-name gap. The close button in the Agents Skills dialog
keeps its “Close dialog” name. Each shared Agent card now names its skills
button for the role, such as “Add skills to engineer,” instead of relying on a
tooltip title. The QA note records the observed interactions and limits of the
pass. The final `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` completed successfully.

## Work and rationale

The task branch already contained the Skills dialog's close-button label fix,
its source-level regression assertion, and an initial QA note. I reviewed these
before making further edits. While tracing the rendered Skills controls, I
found that the shared component used `title="Add skills to agent"` without an
accessible name. A title may appear as a tooltip, but it is not a reliable
programmatic name for assistive technology. Because every applicable built-in
and custom Agent uses the same card component, I added an `aria-label` derived
from `agent.name` there. That names all instances consistently and helps users
distinguish multiple role controls.

The keyboard regression test now guards both the existing close-dialog label
and the role-specific skills-button label. I updated
`docs/qa/2026-11-keyboard-a11y.md` to describe the headless keyboard pass and
the contrast and responsive smoke results. I did not change configuration or
the task's own work file.

For live QA, I started the auth-less server from this task worktree on port
7274. I used Playwright's bundled headless browser, with no system browser
channel or visible window. I loaded Work, Settings, Releases and Agents, then
sent ten Tab key presses per route and recorded the initial focus targets. On
Agents, I continued Tab navigation until reaching “Add skills to engineer,”
opened the Skills dialog with Enter, sent twelve Tab presses and confirmed
focus stayed inside the dialog. Escape dismissed it, and focus returned to the
trigger. The Releases Preview control expands an inline disclosure rather than
a dialog; Escape leaving that preview open was expected.

The final scoped check passed. Remote validation built the tree and ran 185
tests in the changed-path suite; the separate strict timing run passed as well.
Local format, lint, build freshness, CSS layering, theme contrast, hard-coded
color, bare-require and branch-artifact checks passed. The rendered contrast
audit examined 15,292 visible text runs across 16 theme scopes and 14 screen
states and reported no text below the WCAG floor. UI smoke passed at 1440, 390
and 320 pixels in light and dark modes.

## Approaches tried

I first read the current branch version of the task, QA note, component and
test, and checked RepoOS status before changing code. Source inspection showed
the skills button had a tooltip title but no `aria-label`; I kept the fix in
the shared component rather than duplicating labels in each Agent card caller.
The existing test was markup-oriented, so I added a matching assertion for the
shared button's name template.

My first headless WebKit keyboard attempt did not move focus even on a simple
two-button page in this environment. I verified the behavior in that isolated
page and switched to Playwright's bundled headless Chromium. That run handled
Tab, Enter and Escape as expected. The modal check used keyboard presses for
opening, traversing and dismissal; it also checked the trigger regained focus.

The first scoped check stopped at formatting before running tests. I followed
the repository instruction to run `bun run fmt`, then re-ran the check. A later
run was interrupted while I was honoring a request to keep all browser work
headless; I restarted the scoped check after updating the QA note. The final
run completed green, including remote tests, rendered contrast and UI smoke.

## Challenges and blockers

The browser-control provider was unavailable, so the live pass used the
repository's auth-less server and a local headless Playwright browser. WebKit
keyboard input did not traverse focusable elements in this shell, so I used the
bundled Playwright Chromium executable instead. It was launched with
`headless: true` and without a Chrome channel; no user-facing browser window was
opened for the valid pass.

The four route checks focused on initial Tab targets, and the deeper dialog
interaction covered the Skills dialog on Agents. I did not exercise every
dialog or menu elsewhere in those screens. Automated contrast and UI smoke
passed, but they do not prove that every overlay in the application has the
same focus behavior. The QA note keeps this scope clear rather than treating a
single dialog as a universal modal test.

## Key learnings

A `title` attribute can help sighted users but does not guarantee a useful
accessible name. Shared controls should expose an explicit name that includes
context when repeated across similar cards. Testing only markup would not have
confirmed real focus containment or restoration, so the final keyboard check
used actual key presses in a browser and observed the active element after the
dialog closed.

Headless browser choice also matters in this environment: the WebKit browser
launched, but Tab did not move focus even in a minimal page. The bundled
Chromium browser did, without using the user's installed browser. Finally, the
rendered contrast audit covers many theme and screen combinations, while the
manual keyboard pass remains narrower; recording both separately makes the
evidence useful without overstating what was verified.
